name: Pickles
waitingLines: I’m NOT staying just to see {partner}. I’m just... resting. Okay, I’m staying.
Tell {partner} I’m here. Not because I missed them. I’m FINE.

questions.scene: Pickles sniffs your candle, then suddenly starts licking her own back. Then stops.
lines: Don't. Look. At me. It's a hedgehog thing.
questions.question: When hedgehogs find a new smell, they sometimes do what?

choices.label: Sneeze three times for good luck
reply: Cute. Not real. I wish it was.
They actually make frothy spit and lick it onto their spines.
It's called self-anointing. Scientists are still confused.

choices.label: Foam at the mouth and lick it onto their spines
reply: Yes. It's called self-anointing. It's NORMAL.
Nobody knows exactly why. Maybe scent camouflage.
Basil saw me do it on our second date. He stayed. Hero.

choices.label: Write it down in a diary
reply: I DO have a diary. Not the point.
They self-anoint: froth up spit and spread it on their spines.
Very weird. Very hedgehog. Zero explanation.

questions.factBasis: Hedgehogs self-anoint, spreading frothy saliva on their spines.

questions.scene: Pickles pokes a Venus flytrap on your windowsill. It doesn't close. She pokes it again. SNAP.
lines: It WAITED. It counted. That's so me.
questions.question: How does a Venus flytrap avoid snapping shut on raindrops?

choices.label: It can see the bug with tiny eyes
reply: Plants with eyes? Terrifying. No.
It counts touches. Two in a short window triggers the snap.
No eyes. Just math. And snacks.

choices.label: It waits for two touches in a short time
reply: Correct! It literally counts!
Two hair triggers touched within about 20 seconds, then SNAP.
One touch could be nothing. Two means business. I respect that boundary.

choices.label: It only closes at night
reply: Nope, it's open for business all day.
It needs two touches on its trigger hairs within seconds.
A plant with trust issues. Same, flytrap. Same.

questions.factBasis: Venus flytraps typically require two trigger-hair stimulations within ~20–30 seconds to close.

questions.scene: Pickles flinches dramatically at a pinecone on your shelf.
lines: I thought that was a porcupine. Long day.
questions.question: Can a porcupine shoot its quills at you?

choices.label: No, quills come off on contact
reply: Correct. No sniper porcupines.
Quills pop off when touched, and tiny barbs make them stick.
Mine stay on. I'm the safe spiky friend. Mostly.

choices.label: Yes, like darts
reply: Nope. Myth. Movies lied to you.
Porcupines can't shoot quills. They just detach easily on contact.
Back into one and you'll learn. Painfully.

choices.label: Only when it's really mad
reply: Mad or not, no shooting.
Quills detach on contact. Barbs make them hard to pull out.
Rule one: don't hug a porcupine. Rule two: see rule one.

questions.factBasis: Porcupines can't shoot quills; barbed quills detach on contact.

questions.scene: Pickles grabs your hand, holds it for a second, then lets go and crosses her arms.
lines: That was a test. For science. Don't make it a thing.
questions.question: What did a famous study find about holding a partner's hand during stress?

choices.label: It made people sweat more
reply: Rude to sweaty hands everywhere. No.
Holding a partner's hand reduced brain responses to threat.
Hand-holding is basically a chill pill. Free. No prescription.

choices.label: It did nothing at all
reply: It did SOMETHING. Don't be a cactus.
Holding a partner's hand calmed brain responses to stress.
Even more than holding a stranger's hand. Basil is very smug about this.

choices.label: It calmed the brain's threat response
reply: YES. Science says holding hands helps.
In the study, holding a partner's hand reduced brain activity linked to threat.
So when Basil grabs my hand, it's medical. Not cute. Medical.

questions.factBasis: Coan et al. (2006): spousal hand-holding attenuated neural threat responses.

questions.scene: Pickles pokes a cactus on your windowsill and gasps.
lines: A fellow spiky queen.
questions.question: What are cactus spines, technically?

choices.label: Hardened hairs
reply: Close in vibe, wrong in biology.
Cactus spines are modified leaves.
No big leaves means less water lost in the desert. Smart.

choices.label: Tiny bones
reply: Bones?? In a plant?? Spooky.
They're modified leaves.
Tiny spines lose less water and say 'back off' to hungry animals.

choices.label: Modified leaves
reply: Correct. Leaves that chose violence.
Spines lose less water than leaves and guard the plant from snackers.
Honestly? Relatable. Protect yourself, queen.

questions.scene: Pickles shows you a photo of a tiny hedgehog wearing a sock, then hides her face.
lines: It's not cute. It's SO cute. Ugh.
questions.question: What's a baby hedgehog called?

choices.label: A hedgie
reply: Close. Cute. Not official.
It's a hoglet. Yes, really.
Hoglets are born with soft spines under their skin, so mom doesn't get poked.

choices.label: A hoglet
reply: YES. Hoglet. Say it again. Hoglet.
Their spines are tucked under a fluid-filled skin at birth.
Then they pop through within hours. Spiky from day one.

choices.label: A spikelet
reply: That's a grass part. But I love it.
Baby hedgehogs are hoglets.
Their spines are soft and covered at birth. Nature's bubble wrap.

questions.factBasis: Baby hedgehogs are hoglets; spines emerge shortly after birth.

questions.scene: Pickles stares at a deep-sea documentary on your TV in horror.
lines: That's not romantic. That's a hostage situation.
questions.question: What do males of some anglerfish species do after finding a mate?

choices.label: Fuse permanently to her body
reply: Correct. Permanently attached. Forever. Literally.
The tiny male bites on and their bodies fuse, sharing her bloodstream.
And Basil thinks I'M clingy. HA.

choices.label: Write her a love song
reply: In the deep sea? With what pen?
The tiny male latches on and fuses to her body permanently.
Commitment level: absolutely unhinged.

choices.label: Swim away immediately
reply: The opposite. Terrifyingly opposite.
He bites on and fuses with her, forever.
Some females carry several males. Nobody talks about this enough.

questions.factBasis: In some anglerfish (e.g., Ceratiidae), males permanently fuse to females (sexual parasitism).

questions.scene: Pickles holds up a rose and looks at you very seriously.
lines: Rose question. Do NOT make a pun about my name.
questions.question: Botanists say roses don't have true thorns. What do they have?

choices.label: Spikes
reply: Close. Botanists are pickier.
Roses technically have prickles, from the outer skin layer.
Yes. Prickles. Basil laughed for ten minutes.

choices.label: Prickles
reply: Yes. Roses have PRICKLES. I'm in this question.
Thorns grow from deeper stem tissue. Rose prickles come from the outer skin layer.
So technically, roses are named after me. Kidding. Unless?

choices.label: Splinters
reply: Ow. No.
Roses technically have prickles, not thorns.
Prickles grow from the outer layer, so they snap off easily.

questions.scene: Pickles bites into a chili pepper, turns red, and fans her mouth furiously.
lines: I'm FINE. It's FINE. Birds don't even feel this. Unfair.
questions.question: Why can birds eat spicy chili peppers without feeling the burn?

choices.label: Their bodies don't react to capsaicin, the spicy chemical
reply: Correct! Spice-proof!
Birds lack the receptor response that makes chili feel hot to mammals.
So they eat peppers and spread the seeds. Smart pepper. Evil pepper.

choices.label: They drink milk afterward
reply: Birds with milk mustaches? No.
Birds simply don't feel capsaicin's burn the way mammals do.
They spread chili seeds far away. Nature's delivery service.

choices.label: They swallow without tasting
reply: Not the reason, though they do gulp.
Their bodies don't respond to capsaicin, so no burn.
Peppers might have evolved spice to keep mammals away. Rude. Effective.

questions.factBasis: Birds' TRPV1 receptors are insensitive to capsaicin; birds disperse chili seeds.

questions.scene: Pickles looks into a mirror, then at you, then back at the mirror, eyes wide.
lines: My pupils are huge right now. It's the lighting. Not the snacks. Not Basil.
questions.question: What can make your pupils get bigger, besides darkness?

choices.label: Eating something sour
reply: Sour makes you squint, not dilate.
Interest and emotional arousal can make pupils widen.
Your eyes are snitches. Remember that.

choices.label: Blinking really fast
reply: Just makes you look suspicious.
Pupils can widen when you see something exciting or attractive.
Eyes: the worst at keeping secrets.

choices.label: Looking at something or someone you find really interesting
reply: Correct. Interest makes pupils widen.
Emotional arousal, like attraction or excitement, can dilate pupils.
Basil says my pupils go huge around him. Lies. Probably. Ugh.

questions.factBasis: Pupil dilation reflects emotional/cognitive arousal, including interest and attraction.

questions.scene: Pickles hides her hands in her sleeves when you mention Basil.
lines: Hypothetical question. NOT about me and Basil.
questions.question: PDA: hold hands in public, or keep it subtle?

choices.label: Hold hands in public
reply: Hold hands? Bold. Cute. Ugh.
Basil tried once. I rolled into a ball. Progress.

choices.label: Keep it subtle
reply: Subtle. Respect. That's me.
Cool on the outside, screaming on the inside.

A:A: You both hold hands in public. Disgusting. I love it.
So you and {partner} are a walking rom-com.
Sigh. I'm FINE.
A:B: Subtle for you. {partner} wants to hold hands.
Their hand will keep drifting toward yours.
Hold it for three seconds. Then act casual. Trust me.
B:A: You want to hold hands. {partner} likes subtle.
Try pinky fingers. Barely counts as PDA.
Basil and I started there. Now it's full palm.
B:B: You both keep it subtle. Secret agents of love.
Just one eyebrow wiggle between you and {partner}. Everyone else misses it.
Super cute. Super sneaky.

questions.scene: Pickles mutters 'pumpkin' under her breath, then looks horrified.
lines: I didn't say anything.
questions.question: Pet names: cute nicknames, or just real names?

choices.label: Cute nicknames
reply: Nicknames? Sweet pea, honey bun, everything.
Basil calls me 'Pickle.' I pretend to hate it.

choices.label: Just real names
reply: Real names. Classy.
Your name is a name. That's romance.

A:A: Both nickname people. Prepare for 'sugar plum.'
Honestly, you and {partner} will invent ten new ones a month.
The weirder, the cuter. Rules.
A:B: Real names for you. {partner} loves nicknames.
They'll call you 'bean' at some point. Brace.
Smile through it. It's love. Sticky, sticky love.
B:A: Nicknames for you. {partner} likes real names.
Start small. 'Babe.' Watch their face.
If they blush, upgrade to 'honey bun.'
B:B: Both real names. Straight shooters.
When {partner} says your name, it lands. Simple.
Respect. No 'snookums' crisis here.

questions.scene: Pickles holds her phone, thumb hovering over 'send', for a very long time.
lines: This is a theoretical fight. I'm FINE.
questions.question: After a fight, who should text first?

choices.label: Whoever was wrong
reply: Whoever was wrong. Fair. Rare.
But who admits it? Not me.

choices.label: Whoever's less stubborn
reply: Less stubborn. Smart. Mature.
Being stubborn is my cardio though.

choices.label: Whoever gets hungry first
reply: Hungry first. Honestly genius.
Hunger ends wars. Snacks are diplomacy.

A:A: Whoever was wrong. You both agree.
Now you and {partner} just have to agree on who was wrong.
Good luck. Get snacks.
A:B: You say less stubborn. {partner} says whoever's wrong.
So you're saying THEY'RE stubborn. Bold.
Text first. Prove you're the chill one.
A:C: Hunger rule for you. {partner} wants whoever was wrong.
They want an apology. You want snacks.
B:A: You say whoever's wrong. {partner} says whoever's less stubborn.
Plot twist: that might be the same person.
Text first and call it 'being the bigger hedgehog.'
B:B: Less stubborn first. You both agree.
So you and {partner} just have to admit who's stubborn.
Ha. Ha. Ha. Good luck.
B:C: Hunger rule for you. {partner} picks less stubborn.
Bring fries to the negotiation. Win-win.
C:A: You say whoever's wrong. {partner} says whoever's hungry.
They just want snacks. Let them win this one.
C:B: Less stubborn for you. {partner} picks hunger.
Stubborn people still get hungry. That's just science.
Wait an hour. They'll text 'want food?' That's their sorry.
C:C: Hunger rule for both of you. Brilliant.
I can picture it: you and {partner} will make up over pizza every time.
Best fight resolution system. I'm stealing it.

questions.scene: Pickles stares at her phone screen. Three dots appear. Disappear. Appear.
lines: WHY does Basil type so slow. Unrelated. Totally unrelated.
questions.question: Texting: instant replies, or reply whenever?

choices.label: Instant replies
reply: Instant. A hero.
Read receipts on, nerves of steel.

choices.label: Reply whenever
reply: Whenever. A free spirit.
I wish I was this chill.

A:A: Instant replies from both of you. A speedrun couple.
Pretty sure you and {partner} text faster than you talk.
Your phones must be tired.
A:B: You reply whenever. {partner} replies instantly.
They're refreshing the chat. Be kind.
Send a quick 'busy, love you.' Instant peace.
B:A: You reply instantly. {partner} replies whenever.
You'll stare at the screen. Don't spiral.
Put the phone down. They'll text. Probably with a meme.
B:B: Both reply whenever. Calm, collected icons.
Lowkey, you and {partner} trust the silence. Amazing.
I could never. Teach me.

questions.scene: Pickles hugs a pillow, then rolls up around it.
lines: Cuddle question. This is NOT personal research.
questions.question: Cuddling: big spoon or little spoon?

choices.label: Big spoon
reply: Big spoon. Protector energy.
Careful. Some of us are spiky.

choices.label: Little spoon
reply: Little spoon. Cozy legend.
Being held is a whole vibe.

A:A: Both big spoons. Uh oh.
You and {partner} will fight for the back position forever.
Take turns. Or invent a spork.
A:B: Little spoon for you. {partner} wants to be big spoon.
Perfect fit. You get held, they get to feel heroic.
Ugh. Too cute. I'm leaving. I'm not leaving. Tell me more.
B:A: Big spoon for you. {partner} wants to be little spoon.
Perfect fit. Like two puzzle pieces, but cuddlier.
Basil and I are the same combo. Except my spikes. He wears a hoodie.
B:B: Both little spoons. Chaos.
Nobody's holding anybody. You and {partner} are just two spoons, sad.
Flip a coin. Winner gets held.

questions.scene: Pickles' cheeks go pink when you compliment her quills.
lines: Stop. I'm not blushing.
questions.question: When your partner gets embarrassed, what happens?
questions.selfQuestion: When you get embarrassed, what happens?

choices.label: Turns red instantly
reply: Red instantly. Tomato mode.
Can't hide it. It's beautiful.

choices.label: Gets extra sassy
reply: Extra sassy. Defense mechanism.
Sass is armor. I would know.

A:A: You go red, and {partner} knew. Tomato twins.
They've seen your face switch colors. They live for it.
Accept it. It's adorable.
A:B: Extra sassy. {partner} thought you'd just blush.
Oops. They'll get the attitude now.
Tell them it means you're flustered. Save yourself.
B:A: You go red. {partner} expected sass.
They're waiting for attitude. Your cheeks already confessed.
Now they know the blush. They'll be chasing it forever. Sorry.
B:B: Extra sass, and {partner} knew.
They know the attitude means you're flustered.
Sass equals blushing, but louder. They speak fluent you.

questions.scene: Pickles snips a thread with scissors, then yelps. She examines a tiny scratch.
lines: I'm FINE. It's barely a scratch. Totally FINE.
questions.question: Your partner gets a tiny paper cut. How do they react?
questions.selfQuestion: You get a tiny paper cut. How do you react?

choices.label: Shrugs it off
reply: Shrugs it off. A legend.
Tiny cut, zero drama.

choices.label: Full drama, needs a bandage
reply: Full drama. Respect the performance.
Paper cuts DO hurt. I said what I said.

choices.label: Requests a kiss to make it better
reply: Kiss it better? Stop. That's adorable.
Cuts heal faster with love. Fact. Probably.

A:A: You shrug it off, and {partner} knew.
Low drama, high tolerance.
Still, let them fuss. It's their love language.
A:B: Full drama for you. {partner} thought you'd shrug.
They expected a shrug. You gave them a three-act tragedy.
Demand the cartoon bandage. You've earned it.
A:C: Kiss it better for you. {partner} thought you'd shrug.
They didn't know you're a softie.
Hold up the finger and pout. They'll get it.
B:A: You shrug it off. {partner} expected full drama.
You surprised them with how chill you are.
Fake one dramatic gasp. For fun.
B:B: Full drama, and {partner} knew.
They already have the bandages ready. The cartoon ones.
Oscar-worthy performance. Over a paper cut. I'd clap.
B:C: Kiss it better for you. {partner} expected drama.
Different kind of drama. Romantic drama.
Tell them. Watch them pucker up instantly.
C:A: You shrug it off. {partner} expected a kiss request.
They were puckered up and everything. You just said 'it's fine.'
Accept the kiss anyway. Free kiss. Never refuse a free kiss.
C:B: Full drama for you. {partner} expected a kiss request.
Close. You want the drama AND the kiss.
Collapse on the couch. Hold out the finger. Wait.
C:C: Gross. Cute. Okay, mostly cute. I'm blushing for you.

questions.scene: Pickles pokes you with one quill, playfully, then pretends she didn't.
lines: That wasn't me.
questions.question: How does your partner react when you tease them?
questions.selfQuestion: How do you react when your partner teases you?

choices.label: Teases back harder
reply: Teases back harder? Love is war.
Nobody wins. Everybody giggles. Basil still owes me a rematch.

choices.label: Pretends to be mad, secretly loves it
reply: Fake mad, secretly loving it? Classic.
Arms crossed. Smile absolutely visible. Fooling no one.

A:A: You tease back harder, and {partner} knew exactly what they were starting.
They poke you on purpose. They WANT the war.
Keep score on the fridge. Loser buys snacks.
A:B: You pretend to be mad. {partner} braced for a counterattack.
They're ready for war, and you just... pout adorably?
Let one tiny grin slip. Watch them realize they won.
B:A: You tease back harder. {partner} expected a cute fake pout.
Plot twist. They poked the wrong hedgehog.
Go easy on them. Or don't. I'm not your mom.
B:B: You fake-pout, and {partner} saw right through it.
They can see the smile fighting its way out behind your crossed arms.
The mad act was never convincing. Not once. Sorry.

questions.scene: Pickles rolls into a ball when you get close, then peeks out.
lines: Sorry. Reflex. My walls are, um, physical.
questions.question: What gets through your partner's walls fastest?
questions.selfQuestion: What gets through your walls fastest?

choices.label: A silly joke
reply: A silly joke. Laugh first, open up later.
Humor is the key. I know.

choices.label: A long hug
reply: A long hug. Even spiky ones need it.
Hold on. Ouch. Worth it.

A:A: Silly jokes work on you, and {partner} knew.
They know your walls are made of giggles and bad puns.
One knock-knock joke and the drawbridge just drops. Embarrassing. Cute.
A:B: Hugs get through your walls. {partner} guessed jokes.
They're doing stand-up when you need arms.
Tell them: less comedy, more cuddles.
B:A: Jokes get through your walls. {partner} guessed hugs.
They're hugging when they should be joking.
Hug AND joke. Double defense breach.
B:B: Long hugs work on you, and {partner} knew.
They know you melt in hug number two.
Spiky outside, marshmallow inside.

questions.scene: Pickles stomps in grumpy, then instantly softens when she sees your snacks.
lines: Grumpy question. I'm not grumpy. I'm FINE.
questions.question: When your partner is grumpy, what fixes it?
questions.selfQuestion: When you're grumpy, what fixes it?

choices.label: Food
reply: Food. Hangry is a real condition. I've had it since birth.
Feed first, feelings later.

choices.label: Ten minutes alone
reply: Ten minutes alone. A reset button.
Do not disturb. Do not even breathe loudly.

choices.label: Being annoyingly cute at them
reply: Annoyingly cute? High risk, high reward.
Could fix everything. Could start a war.

A:A: Food fixes you, and {partner} knew.
There's probably an emergency granola bar in their bag right now. For you.
That's not a snack. That's a love letter.
A:B: Alone time fixes you. {partner} guessed food.
They keep feeding you when you need quiet.
Take the snack. Then leave.
A:C: Annoying cuteness fixes you. {partner} guessed food.
They're bringing snacks. You secretly want them to be obnoxiously adorable at you.
Next grumpy day, just say: 'Do the cute thing.' Watch them deliver.
B:A: Food fixes you. {partner} guessed alone time.
They leave you alone when you need a sandwich.
Tell them: snacks first, space second.
B:B: Ten minutes alone, and {partner} knew.
They know to back away slowly when your eyebrows do the thing.
Healthy. It's not rejection, it's maintenance.
B:C: Annoying cuteness fixes you. {partner} guessed alone time.
They keep leaving when they should stay.
Grab them. Say 'be cute at me.'
C:A: They're being adorable at a hungry person. Dangerous.
Rule of the house: feed first, cute second. Write it on the fridge.
C:B: Alone time fixes you. {partner} guessed cuteness.
They're being cute too close. Too soon.
C:C: Annoyingly cute works on you, and {partner} knew.
One silly face from them and your grump just collapses.
You're a total softie. I'm the same. Don't tell anyone.
